newsitem.title: UK: Euro bourses claw back losses but still down.
newsitem.headline: Euro bourses claw back losses but still down.

text.p: European stocks clawed back some losses on Friday but remained badly rattled by volatility on Wall Street which opened lower after a big drop the previous day.

On currency markets, the dollar was down against the mark after stronger-than-expected German economic data on Thursday dampened speculation of a cut in interest rates and boosted the German currency.

London, Frankfurt and Paris, which have all hit peaks in recent weeks. showed big losses in early trade after New York posted a 1.32 percent decline at the close on Thursday. They regained some poise later but New York's unsteady start today did little to help.
"The feeling is that we are very much at the top of the range and the market is going to be volatile," said one dealer in London.
Europe's major bourses, which have largely mirrored the bull run in New York, were unsettled by Wall Street's weakness which only two days ago touched a record of 7,067.46 on the Dow Jones average.

Wall Street investors became nervous about an upturn in long-term interest rates and the weaker dollar. The currency's recent strength has been a big factor in the stock market's rally, drawing in investment to U.S. financial markets from outside the country.
London, Europe's biggest bourse, was hardest hit by Wall Street, falling by 0.8 percent but recovering a little by mid-afternoon.

But dealers said the market was still underpinned by bid speculation. Shares in Cadbury Schweppes Plc were up 8-1/2p to 493-1/2 on renewed bid speculation, with Unilever Plc seen as a possible predator, dealers said.

Frankfurt ended floor trading 11.94 points down at 3,184.09 on the DAX index after trading around one hundred points off recent record highs. But dealers said the pause was probably only a breather before another rally next week.
"Wall Street closing lower overnight didn't help and the weaker bond market has also had an impact," a trader said.
The dollar's weakness, though stabilising during the session, also hurt exporters' stocks. "The dollar doesn't really know where to go now," a trader said.

"I really think this is just going to be just a little breather before we head on upwards again next week. I still think this market needs a correction, but there are still no real signs of it," he said.
In Paris, almost every stock in the CAC-40 leading share index turned downwards in early trade but the market regained some poise and was down only a few points by mid-afternoon.
On the currency front, the dollar was depressed as expectations diminished of near-term German interest rate cuts and attitudes to the yen turned cautiously more positive, analysts said.

"The bias is towards a firmer mark in the aftermath of yesterday's (German) numbers...running parallel is the more positive yen sentiment that is prevailing in Japan," said Tim Fox, treasury economist at Standard Chartered in London.

On the yen side, senior Japanese Finance Ministry official Eisuke Sakakibara said overnight that foreigners had been buying yen since February 20, and forex rates had been "rather stable" since the G7 meeting of leading industrial countries this month.
The dollar slipped about half a pfennig and half a yen during the European session although on a broader canvas the market still saw bullish scenario for the American currency, analysts said.
Currency dealers said there was not much to stir the U.S. currency before Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's Humphrey-Hawkins testimony next week, analysts said.

The dollar made no immediate reaction to Greenpan's speech on Friday when he cautioned against over-regulating financial markets, adding the Fed's ability to intercept potential systemic risks should not be impeded.

Traders spent the morning awaiting the EU's ruling on Italy's controversial euro tax, designed to cut its budget deficit for monetary union. The tax was approved but it matched expectations and had scant impact on the lira.
CURRENCIES AT 1545 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 1.6830 marks and 122.75 yen compared to the 1.6895 and 123.07 in late European trade on Thursday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1545 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was down 24.5 points at 4,331.6.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was down 4.32 ints at 2,570.92.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index closed down 11.94 points at 3,184.09.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed in the afternoon at $353.30 an ounce, compared with $346.45 at the London close on Thursday. Silver was at $5.26, up six cents.
